_README.what: Investigations replace the quest board. One investigation per story arc; each accretes exhibits, threads and leads as sessions are played.
_README.why: The quest board carried 73 entries, 25 of which had no description at all. A board answers 'what could we do next'. An investigation answers 'what is happening to us'.
_README.route: #/investigations for the index, #/investigation/<id> for a file. #/quests and #/quest/<id> redirect here.
_README.authoring: See docs/INVESTIGATIONS.md. Every claim in a brief must be pinned to a numbered exhibit that exists in props.json with a chain of custody.
_README.tone: Heavy Waluigi analysis, light story prose. The story is in events.json; this system is the archivist arguing about the story.

exhibit_shape.propId: id in data/props.json - renders the physical document via the existing exhibit engine
exhibit_shape.session: id of an entry in the investigation's sessions[]
exhibit_shape.visual: inline-CSS specimen art. Inline styles only - no classes, no ASCII, so the art travels with the data.
exhibit_shape.dc: the single examination DC for this exhibit (d6+1 vs dc)
exhibit_shape.analysis: the archivist's full reading, revealed by one successful examination. `## ` starts a subheading.

_README.dice: Two rolls, both taken from archiecourtcase. (1) EXAMINATION: one d6+1 vs the exhibit's dc, once per exhibit, revealing the whole analysis. (2) INSIGHT: inline [[roll:DC|text|success|failure]] spans anywhere in onRecord or analysis, rolled as a plain d6, once each. There is no layer ladder, no re-rolling and no XP - you roll to learn things, not to farm them. Every result is remembered in localStorage; the only way back is the file's reset link.
_README.storage: Per-browser in localStorage under 'waluipedia-investigations-v1', shaped { invId: { exam:{exhibitId:'success'|'failure'}, insight:{rollId:'success'|'failure'} } }. Nothing is written back to JSON.

quest_migration.note: quests.json is retained read-only as the historical campaign log. Nothing was deleted from it.

investigations.title: Three Houses, One Method
investigations.subtitle: The anchor, the graft, and the question of who keeps the record
investigations.imageCaption: No images survive of any of the three houses. Waluigi asked. Multiple times. One of the three replied, which was worse.
investigations.hook: Three ruined houses, one load-bearing noun, and a diary page instructing the reader to watch whoever is keeping the record. Waluigi keeps the record.
investigations.brief:
Waluigi has opened one file instead of seventy-three.

The reason is arithmetic. The old quest board carried seventy-three entries, and Waluigi has now read all of them in one sitting, which is a thing Waluigi will not be doing again. Twenty-five were requests with no description at all — a title, a location, a notional reward, and nothing else. Several more were of the form *a farmer has lost a screw*. Waluigi does not object to a farmer losing a screw. Waluigi objects to filing it beside the destruction of a bloodline.

A board is the wrong instrument. A board answers the question *what could we do next*, and the party has never once been short of things to do next. The question the party is actually short of is **what is happening to us**, and that question is not answered by a list. It is answered by paper: things that were written down at the time by people who did not know what they were part of.

So this is an investigation. One per arc. It accretes.

## What this file is arguing

Three houses have failed in the same way, and Waluigi is prepared to argue they failed by the same method.

The **Shadeward**, where Archie woke on marble in a world with no colour and no fire, and where the way out turned out to be a *shadow anchor* — an object holding a plane's condition in place over a house.

The **Feyward**, where the manor stopped attacking people and started converting them: a Toad who lost time standing at a door, a Lady replaced by overgrowth wearing her own face, a construct that rusted at the speed the house rusts things, and Mystic Morel coming out of a wall to say *don't make Toad Lee the anchor*.

The **ruined manor** near the Thornwood, where Agent L kicked aside a rug and found a teleportation circle deliberately damaged — or made to appear damaged — and where a spirit called Ashford said the Crown's bloodline was *broken at third branch*.

Anchor. Anchor. Branch. Graft.

Four words from four different mouths in three different houses, and all four of them are engineering vocabulary from the same discipline: something is held fixed so that something else can be pulled onto it, and the join is described in the language of gardening so that nobody at the table has to say what it is.

Waluigi is not claiming a conspiracy. Waluigi is claiming a **contractor** — a method, repeated, by someone who has done it before and writes it down. And per the Aurelian diary page, the method's central instruction is not about bodies at all. It is *watch who is keeping the record*.

## Why the reader has to roll

Every claim above is Waluigi's. Waluigi is a magnificent and interested party, and an interested party's summary is worth exactly nothing without the paper underneath it.

So the paper is here. Twelve exhibits, each one a physical article with a custody chain, most of them written by people who had no idea they were producing evidence — an ammunition sheet, an unpaid invoice, a salvage return with the values struck out, a card-reading register whose last outcome column is deliberately blank.

Examining an exhibit is a roll because analysis is a skill and the archive is not going to pretend otherwise. A failed examination is not a locked door; it means the reader did not get anything new out of it *this time*, and the paper is still on the table tomorrow.

Deeper layers cost more and pay more. The third layer of most exhibits is where the uncomfortable reading lives, and Waluigi has put the uncomfortable reading in writing rather than keeping it in Waluigi's head, for reasons the seal rubbing explains at length.

## Standing rule of this file

When a document can be read two ways, the archive files **both**, and marks which one the archive prefers.

Kamek read a dedication as a personal address, wrote *for me* on it in charcoal, and the label lost first and then everyone else did. Waluigi is not immune to this. Waluigi is simply writing the preference down, where somebody can check it later.

WAH.

threads.title: The anchor is a role, not an object
threads.text: A shadow anchor held a plane's condition over the Shadeward estate. Morel warned against making Toad Lee *the* anchor — definite article, technical usage. The Black Crystal is filed in the party's own paperwork as an **anchor key**. If the role can be filled by a person, the party is currently escorting both a candidate and a key.

threads.title: Grafting is succession fraud with a biological delivery mechanism
threads.text: Aurelian's diary: what is joined is not the flesh, it is the **line**, and a line joined once can be joined again. The false Lady was not an impostor pretending — on the document's own logic she was a legitimate graft onto an opened line. The Ashford spirit's “broken at third branch” puts the same vocabulary inside the succession crisis.

threads.title: Whoever keeps the record decides afterwards what happened
threads.text: The method's own instruction, written by one of its architects. It makes the Waluipedia a target and a compromised archivist indistinguishable from a diligent one. Countermeasure: every claim pinned to a numbered exhibit with a chain of hands. Do not believe Waluigi. Roll against the paper.

threads.title: There is administration behind this
threads.text: The Umbral Signet grants **estate authority** — a credential, meaningless without a system that recognises it. The Shadeward butler knew Cornelius was expecting visitors who arrived by accident from another plane. A house does not expect an accident; somebody sent notice ahead. The closest thing to a suspect in this file is a clerical department, which Waluigi finds worse than a lich.

threads.title: The originals may still be inside
threads.text: Destroying the false Lady produced a ring with, allegedly, the real one in it. If the graft is a container rather than a replacement, every grafted figure across three houses may still have somebody in it. The party has checked one.

leads.title: Verify the occupant of the OC Soul Ring
leads.objective: Establish, with the Mirror of True Reflection and not with hope, whether the ring lodged with the Anvil actually contains Lady Aurelian.
leads.why: The entire container thesis rests on one unverified claim, and the party wants it to be true, which is precisely when verification stops happening. The mirror exists, it is repaired, and it has never been assigned a keeper.

leads.title: Account for Toad Lee's missing time
leads.objective: Reconstruct where Toad Lee was, and with whom, during the period he cannot explain — without telling him he is a suspect, because he may be a victim and the two require different handling.
leads.why: Morel warned specifically against making him the anchor, using the grammar of an instruction to the party rather than a warning about an enemy. Either he was intercepted or he is a vector. Nobody has done the work.

leads.title: Determine whether Steely's core retains memory
leads.objective: Establish whether the fragmented core housing in Hjumpik's pack can be read, before deciding whether it should be — the salvage return says memory *unverified*, not destroyed.
leads.why: Steely was in the Feyward manor during Toad Lee's missing time, could not lie, and could not be enchanted into forgetting the way a Toad can. He is the most credible witness the branch ever had and he is currently loose parts.

leads.title: Identify the card removed from the Oracle's Deck
leads.objective: Find out which card is missing from Remi's deck and who took it, before the sixth outcome column fills itself in.
leads.why: Somebody edited a record inside the party's own pocket — the same operational signature as everything else in this file. The next draw is *The Ring*, and there is currently a ring in evidence with a person allegedly inside it.

leads.title: Establish the fourth item of the Portal Set
leads.objective: Name and locate item four. Three are catalogued in full; the set is a routing system and one function is unaccounted for.
leads.why: Authority to enter, an anchor to fix the far end, an instrument to verify what arrived — the only job left in the sequence is deciding what a traveller *is* when it comes through. If that is what item four does, it is the graft's machinery.

leads.title: Recover full plans of the ruined manor teleportation circle
leads.objective: Obtain the complete geometry. The archive holds partial sketches only, and partial geometry cannot answer whether the damage was sabotage or camouflage.
leads.why: Sections were scratched out and connections severed. Either somebody ensured it could never be used again, or somebody made it *look* unusable while preserving its function for people who know how to restore it. Those two readings have opposite consequences.

leads.title: Trace the Mirror's absent fragment
leads.objective: Establish where the missing piece was recovered from and who separated it from the frame in Usk's private chambers.
leads.why: A truth instrument was found broken with one piece elsewhere. Akamatsu billed 150 gold to recover and refit it. Waluigi would like to know whether it was lost or *taken*, because those are different crimes and only one of them has a suspect.

leads.title: Find the register of estate authority
leads.objective: Identify who maintains the record of shadow estate credentials — the system that makes the Umbral Signet mean anything.
leads.why: A credential requires an issuer. Waluigi has been calling this the clerical department for want of a name, and a nameless suspect is an unfalsifiable one, which is Waluigi's least favourite kind.

leads.title: Establish what Mystic Morel is owed
leads.objective: Determine the price of the key before Morel names it at a moment of Morel's choosing.
leads.why: Morel came out of a wall, threw a key underarm so it could not be refused, issued a warning phrased as a technical instruction, and left. Nobody does that for nothing. The debt exists whether or not the party has written it down, so the party should write it down.

leads.title: Confirm the seal carried no variance
leads.objective: Have an actual ward scholar — Waluigi has said on the record that Waluigi is not one — confirm that the outer ring repeats without variation, and that the inner mark dedicates the prison to its occupant.
leads.why: The single most consequential misreading in the campaign rests on notation Waluigi cannot personally verify. If Waluigi is wrong about the variance, several conclusions in this file need withdrawing, and Waluigi would rather withdraw them than defend them.

exhibits.title: The Key That Was Thrown
exhibits.secured: 23 Harvestide, 1040 BF · Feyward manor, mid-corridor, in flight
exhibits.onRecord: Mystic Morel came out of a wall, threw [[roll:4|a warm brass key|warm means carried against a body, not lifted off a hook on the way past. Morel had been holding it for a while.|brass takes heat off anything. It proves nothing on its own.]] underarm without stopping, said one sentence, and was gone. Hjumpik caught the key. Two hearers agree on the sentence.
exhibits.analysis:
## What the tag actually records

Waluigi wants the reader to notice what this exhibit is. It is not a key. The key is in Hjumpik's pocket and Waluigi has never held it. The exhibit is the **tag** — and the tag records a method of transfer, which is the part everybody skips.

Morel did not hand the key over. Handing something over creates a moment: two people, one object, an exchange that can be witnessed, refused, negotiated, or retracted. Morel threw it. Underarm. Without stopping. That converts a negotiation into a delivery, and a delivery cannot be refused — Hjumpik's only options were [[roll:3|catch or drop|Morel threw it to the dwarf who had just healed him off the floor. He was not testing reflexes. He was paying a debt to the only person present who had treated him as a patient rather than a suspect.|even odds either way; anyone might have caught it.]], and Morel already knew which one Hjumpik would pick.

Waluigi files this as the first competent thing Mystic Morel has done on the record.

## The sentence, read as an instruction rather than a warning

“Don't make Toad Lee the anchor.”

Everyone in the party heard that as protective. Waluigi has read it eleven times and Waluigi does not think it is protective. It is **technical**. A warning would have been *they're going to hurt Toad Lee*. An instruction is *don't do the thing you are about to do*, and the thing named is a procedure, with a role in it, and [[roll:5|the role has a name: anchor|role-names belong to procedures with more than one participant. Somebody else in that procedure is the operator.|could be a figure of speech Morel picked up second-hand.]].

Which means Morel knows the procedure. Which means Morel has seen the procedure performed, or has performed it, or has been briefed by someone who has. None of the three readings is comfortable and Waluigi is not going to pretend otherwise.

Also note the grammar. Not *don't let them make Toad Lee the anchor*. **Don't make.** Morel was warning the party about the party.

## Anchor, three houses — the reason this investigation exists

Waluigi opened this entire file because of one word appearing in three places that have no business sharing vocabulary.

**Shadeward.** Archie got his fire back by smashing a *shadow anchor* — an object holding a plane's condition in place over a house.

**Feyward.** Morel warns against making a *person* the anchor.

**The ruined manor.** A teleportation circle, damaged in a way that reads as deliberate, that would need something to hold its far end steady.

Three houses. One load-bearing noun. Waluigi is aware that a word can be a coincidence, and Waluigi has been careful to say so wherever this file makes a claim. But an anchor is a specific engineering idea: it is the thing that stays fixed so that something else can pull against it. If the same technique is being used in the Shadowfell, in the Feyward, and under a rug near the Thornwood, then this is not three hauntings. It is [[roll:6|one contractor|contractors reuse suppliers. If the method is shared, the components were bought from the same place, and purchases leave invoices.|shared vocabulary is not shared employment.]].

Waluigi does not know who the contractor is. Waluigi knows the contractor prefers anchors that can walk, because an anchor that can walk can be persuaded to stand somewhere and then be told it volunteered.

docRolls.match: make Toad Lee the anchor
docRolls.success: Morel names one specific party member and one specific role. He is not warning the party about a monster — he is warning them about an assignment. Somebody, somewhere, has a procedure with a slot in it, and Morel has seen enough of that procedure to know Toad Lee fits the slot.
docRolls.failure: a thief's parting line. He talks in riddles for a living.

docRolls.match: Nobody has tested it
docRolls.success: the party has held a possible exit from that manor since the dark rooms and has never once tried the door. The key is not the unresolved thing here. The willingness to owe Morel something is.
docRolls.failure: no time, no opportunity. Manors are busy.

exhibits.title: The Bag, Emptied Onto A Table
exhibits.secured: 23 Harvestide, 1040 BF · taken down by two hands at once
exhibits.visual:
ITEM ··· CLAIMED BY
HJUMPIK
—
MOREL
watch, stopped
NOBODY. EVERYONE LOOKED AWAY.
exhibits.onRecord: Morel's bag was [[roll:4|emptied and listed by two people simultaneously|a two-scribe inventory is a courtroom habit. Somebody in that room has been deposed before.|sensible practice; plenty of quartermasters do it.]], so that neither could later be accused of editing the list. The third column is claims of ownership. Most of it was filled in after somebody said “wait, that's mine.”
exhibits.analysis:
## Seven unlabelled keys

Line two: *Keys, assorted, unlabelled, 7. Unclaimed.*

A thief carries keys. Fine. A prophet carries keys — less fine, but Morel is both, so still fine. What is **not** fine is *unlabelled*. Seven keys and not one tag, not one scratch mark, not one loop of coloured thread. Waluigi has run a criminal enterprise of some distinction and can report that nobody carries seven unlabelled keys by accident. You label keys because you will forget. Unless forgetting is the point, in which case you label nothing and you memorise, and you memorise because [[roll:5|a written label is a confession that can be taken off your body|which implies Morel expects to be searched, and expects the searcher to be literate and hostile.|standard thief discipline, nothing more.]].

One of those seven, Waluigi notes, is not on the list any more. Morel threw it at Hjumpik.

## The stopped watch that nobody would claim

Two pocket watches. One still running — claimed instantly by Hjumpik, which tells the reader something about Hjumpik and nothing about the case. One stopped. Claimed by, in the exact wording of the inventory: *Nobody. Everyone looked away.*

Waluigi has interrogated professionals who gave less away than that column.

A room full of people who will loot a corpse for supplies without blinking, and a stopped watch produces [[roll:4|a coordinated failure of eye contact|coordinated means more than one person already knew. They had heard the same thing, from the same source, before that day.|people are squeamish about dead men’s watches. It happens.]]. That is not superstition. Superstition is loud. That is **recognition** — several people in that room knew what a stopped watch means in this context, declined to say so, and declined in a way they thought was invisible.

Waluigi does not yet know what it means. Waluigi knows the party is keeping something from its own archive, and Waluigi is writing that down where they can read it.

## An incomplete deck, before the deck was given away

*Cards, prophetic, incomplete deck, 1. Claimed by Morel.*

Hold that against the Reading Register, which Remi keeps for the Oracle's Deck that **Morel gave to Remi as a gift**. Register line five: *Card removed from deck. Not by Remi.*

So. The deck was already incomplete while it was in Morel's bag. Morel then gifted it. Remi, who is diligent to the point of being annoying about it, logged a card as missing and specified that the removal was not hers.

Two possibilities and Waluigi dislikes both.

One: Morel gave away a deck with a card already pulled, meaning the gift was [[roll:6|pre-edited|pre-editing requires knowing which future to remove, which requires having read the deck first. Morel drew from it before gifting it.|decks lose cards. Bags are rough places.]] — somebody decided in advance which future Remi would not be permitted to draw.

Two: the card left after the handover, by a hand that was not Remi's, in a house where things come out of walls.

The register's sixth draw is *The Ring*, outcome column deliberately blank because it has not happened yet. Waluigi would very much like to know which card is missing before the sixth outcome fills itself in.

docRolls.match: Excuses, prepared, written out in advance
docRolls.success: written in advance means anticipating an interrogation he had not yet had. Morel packs for being caught the way other people pack for rain.
docRolls.failure: a performer keeps patter. It is a living.

docRolls.match: Item removed from table during inventory
docRolls.success: seventeen articles logged, one gone, under two pairs of eyes kept precisely so this could not happen. The theft is not the finding — the finding is that Morel can take something off a watched table while the watchers are the ones writing the list.
docRolls.failure: a busy room and a long list. Things move.

exhibits.title: The Grafting Page
exhibits.secured: Feyward manor · loose page, recovered by Toad Lee
exhibits.visual: WHAT IS JOINED IS THE LINE
exhibits.onRecord: A loose page from Lady Aurelian's diary, unsigned beyond the initial. [[roll:3|Toad Lee read it|he read it during the dark-rooms crawl, while Hjumpik was cutting through Sedeia's overgrowth in total blackness. Nobody else in that corridor could see well enough to read anything. The page entered the record through one pair of eyes, and its finder is the one party member who reads the lore.|he read it. That is all the record says.]] while other people were swinging axes at plants.
exhibits.analysis:
## Gardener's vocabulary, chosen on purpose

“They call it **grafting**, which is a gardener's word, and they chose it on purpose.”

Aurelian is telling the reader that the terminology is public relations. A graft is not a wound. A graft *takes*. The tree does not complain afterwards — and the reason she gives for that is the sentence Waluigi keeps rereading: *the tree has nothing left to complain with.*

That is not gardening. That is a description of a survivor with no faculty left for objection. Somebody chose a horticultural euphemism for it and then used the euphemism at a dinner table [[roll:4|until it stopped sounding like anything|then the roll is not about the word, it is about the room. A euphemism only goes soft in company, which means there were repeat listeners — a table of people who heard a house describe cutting a line out of a person, and went on eating. Aurelian names that table twice on this page and never once names who sat at it. That guest list is the missing exhibit in this investigation, and it is missing because the only surviving person who could write it is the woman currently folded into a ring in Steely's smith's keeping.|any word goes soft with use.]].

## What is joined is the line

“What is joined is not the flesh. Anyone can join flesh. What is joined is the **line** — and a line that has been joined once can be joined again.”

Read that as an engineer and not as a poet.

Grafting is not body horror. Grafting is **succession fraud with a biological delivery mechanism**. You do not need to replace a person if you can replace their position in a lineage — and once a bloodline has been spliced successfully, the splice is repeatable, because the hard part was never the second graft. The hard part was establishing that the line tolerates grafting at all.

Which reframes the entire Feyward branch. The false Lady Aurelian was not an impostor in the ordinary sense. An impostor pretends. The overgrowth wearing its owner's face was, on this document's own logic, a *legitimate graft* onto a line that had already been opened.

And it reframes the succession crisis, because the Ashford spirit told Luigi the Crown's bloodline was “[[roll:6|broken at third branch|third branch, third house, item three of four. Waluigi does not like how often the number three is load-bearing in this file.|two houses using a tree metaphor is not a conspiracy.]].” **Branch.** Another gardener's word, from an entirely different house, in an entirely different mouth.

## Watch who keeps the record

The last line is the one that made Waluigi close the folder and go for a walk.

“The Legion watches the wrong end of it. They watch the bodies. The bodies are the least interesting part. Watch the **blood-work**, and watch **who is keeping the record of it**, because whoever keeps that record decides afterwards what happened.”

Waluigi keeps a record. Waluigi is, by trade and by vanity, the person who decides afterwards what happened. Aurelian has written down the exact vulnerability of Waluigi's entire profession and she wrote it before Waluigi ever opened this file.

So Waluigi will state the obvious risk in Waluigi's own archive, because refusing to state it would be the first symptom of the disease: **if the method works by controlling the record, then the Waluipedia is a target, and [[roll:5|a compromised archivist would produce a file that looks exactly like this one|so apply Aurelian's own test to Waluigi. She says watch who keeps the record. This archive is kept by someone who was in the manor, who reads with both hands while a dwarf clears the path, and who has never once filed his own movements as an exhibit.|unfalsifiable either way, which is rather the problem.]].**

The countermeasure is not trust. The countermeasure is that every claim in this investigation is pinned to a numbered exhibit that exists physically, in custody, with a chain of hands attached. Do not believe Waluigi. Roll against the paper.

docRolls.match: the tree has nothing left to complain with
docRolls.success: not "does not complain" — has nothing left to complain with. Aurelian is describing a survivor with the faculty of objection removed. She is writing about the procedure from the inside, and she is not describing it as a death.
docRolls.failure: a gardening image, morbidly put.

docRolls.match: which is the part they do not say aloud at the table
docRolls.success: at the table. Aurelian heard this discussed at dinner, in company, by people comfortable enough to use the euphemism and careful enough to stop short of the repeatable part. This page is a record of a conversation, not a private theory.
docRolls.failure: she may simply mean it is unspoken generally.

docRolls.match: whoever keeps that record decides afterwards what happened
docRolls.success: she wrote this before the overgrowth wore her face, and the party now holds her in a ring while Waluigi writes her file. Aurelian's last instruction was to watch the archivist, and the archivist is the one who filed her.
docRolls.failure: sound advice about record-keeping. Widely applicable.

exhibits.title: Custody Undertaking — The OC Soul Ring
exhibits.secured: 24 Harvestide, 1040 BF · recovered by Bob-omb, indoors, against advice
exhibits.visual:
OC
REPORTED OCCUPANT · THE ACTUAL ONE
exhibits.onRecord: The Lady interviewing Hjumpik over cold tea [[roll:4|was not the Lady|the substitution held through an entire interview over cold tea. Whatever wore her did not merely look like her — it answered questions as her.|it was noticed eventually, which is what matters.]]. What was left after the explosion was a gold ring, heavy, engraved **OC** inside the band, allegedly containing the real Aurelian. The occupant was not consulted, being inside it.
exhibits.analysis:
## The word non-negotiable, three times

The undertaking uses the word *non-negotiable* three times and underlines it once. Waluigi has drafted a great many instruments designed to be quietly negotiable later and can tell the reader from the inside: you repeat a word three times when you expect to be argued with by [[roll:5|somebody specific|the drafter had a name in mind and did not write it. That omission is the only cowardice in an otherwise fearless document.|boilerplate caution, common in custody instruments.]].

The party knew, at the moment of signing, that someone was going to come for this ring. The document is braced for it.

## A person filed as an article

Read the schedule. *Article: Ring, gold, heavy.* *Reported occupant: The Lady of the manor. The actual one.*

The archive has now created a category error and Waluigi is responsible for it. Aurelian is in the exhibit register under **Article**, with a custody chain, a recovery method, and a lodging location, filed exactly as one would file a dagger.

Waluigi has thought about this for some time and Waluigi is going to keep it that way, because the alternative is worse. If she is filed as a person, she gets a status line and sympathy and nobody signs for her. Filed as an article, she gets a **chain of custody** — dated, witnessed, transferable only in writing. The indignity is the protection. Somebody is on the hook by name for where she is at all times.

*Reported* occupant, though. Waluigi wrote that word deliberately. Nobody has verified the ring contains Aurelian. What the party has is a claim, a convenient artefact, and [[roll:4|an enormous appetite for the story being true|and the party has a Mirror of True Reflection sitting in a different exhibit, unused, which would settle it in an afternoon.|hope is not evidence, but it is not a crime either.]].

## Bob-omb, indoors, against advice

Means of recovery: *Bob-omb, indoors, against advice.*

Waluigi wishes to log a tactical objection that the party will ignore. You do not resolve a hostage situation involving a soul-capture article by detonating in an enclosed room. It worked. It worked in the specific way that things work when the universe is being generous to people it intends to bill later.

But here is the analytical point, and it is not about safety. **The false Lady's destruction produced the ring.** The overgrowth wearing Aurelian's face was, on the grafting page's own logic, joined to her line — and when the graft was blown apart, what fell out was the original, portable, and conveniently pocket-sized.

Which means the graft was not a replacement. It was a **container with a person still in it**. That is either the most encouraging fact in this file — the originals survive the procedure, they can be recovered — or the most alarming one, because it means every grafted figure in three houses may still have someone inside, and [[roll:6|the party has so far checked exactly one|the Shadeward butler. Cornelius. The false Aurelian. None were tested for an occupant, and two of them are no longer available to test.|one is more than most parties would manage.]].

docRolls.match: The Lady of the manor. The actual one.
docRolls.success: the drafter distinguishes the occupant from the thing recovered, which means the archive accepted that both existed at once — a real Aurelian inside the ring and a false one answering questions over cold tea for an entire interview.
docRolls.failure: a clarification, carefully worded.

docRolls.match: Bob-omb, indoors, against advice
docRolls.success: the means of recovery is filed as plainly as the article. Whoever drafted this expected the recovery to be challenged later and made sure the reckless part was already on the record rather than discovered on it.
docRolls.failure: an accurate and unflattering description of a Tuesday.

FILED, THEN MADE TO SAY NO
exhibits.onRecord: Steely rusted down and exploded. Hjumpik filed the remains on a salvage return and [[roll:3|struck out every recoverable value|striking a value leaves it readable. Hjumpik refused the salvage without concealing what the salvage was worth.|a refusal is a refusal.]] on the sheet.
exhibits.analysis:
## The format is the argument

This is a **salvage return**. It is the standard form for recovering value from a destroyed construct: component, condition, salvage value. Three columns, all business.

Hjumpik filled it in correctly and then struck out the third column on every line. Frame sections: recoverable, struck. Plating: recoverable, struck. Core housing: *fragmented, memory unverified*, recoverable, struck.

He did not refuse to file. He filed, and then [[roll:4|made the filing say no|he used the enemy’s own form against the enemy’s own procedure. Waluigi has taught this technique and never seen it improvised.|he simply did not want the parts sold.]]. Waluigi respects this more than Waluigi is prepared to say in a public document.

## Memory unverified

Two words in the condition column and nobody has followed them up: **memory unverified.**

A construct's core housing holds its memory. Steely was present for the corridors, the overgrowth, the doors that should not have opened, and — critically — Steely was present in the same house as Toad Lee during the period Toad Lee cannot account for.

Steely could not lie. Steely also could not be enchanted into forgetting in the way a Toad can. Which makes the fragmented core the single most credible witness the Feyward branch ever had, and it is currently loose parts in a pack.

Waluigi is not asking the party to disturb the burial. Waluigi is noting, for the record and with as much delicacy as Waluigi possesses, that *unverified* is not the same as *destroyed*, and that [[roll:5|somebody wrote it that way on purpose|and an unverified core can be read by an artificer. There is one in this file, owed 650 gold, who has not pressed for payment.|a fragmented core is usually a dead one.]].

## Why a rusting dog is filed in a succession-fraud case

A reader may reasonably ask why a construct's death sits in a file about grafting, anchors, and three ruined houses.

Because of *how* Steely died. Not shattered. Not cut down. **Rusted** — progressive, visible, over a period, in a house where the overgrowth is advancing and the Revel is still singing. Steely degraded at the pace the manor degrades things, and then went up near a foot-washing scene that nobody has adequately explained either.

The Feyward manor is not attacking intruders. It is **converting** them: Toad Lee loses time, the Lady is replaced by growth wearing her face, Waluigi needs sprites to put him back together, and the metal dog oxidises like it has been left out for a season. Every one of those is the same process at a different speed against a different material.

Steely is in this file because [[roll:6|Steely is the timer|then the rate is measurable, and the party spent weeks in that house without measuring anything. Ask how fast Toad Lee is going.|rust is rust; constructs corrode.]]. He is the only party member whose rate of conversion could be watched with the naked eye, and the party watched it, and did not read it as data until it was a pile in a pack.

docRolls.match: Fragmented; memory unverified
docRolls.success: unverified is not destroyed. A fragmented core with unread memory is a witness nobody has interviewed — and there is an artificer in this same file, owed 650 gold, who works on exactly this kind of instrument.
docRolls.failure: a fragmented core is usually a dead one.

docRolls.match: collected the pieces by hand at the site
docRolls.success: by hand, at the site, then filed as a complete return with every value struck. Hjumpik did the paperwork correctly specifically so that his refusal could not be recorded as an oversight.
docRolls.failure: he did not want the parts sold. That is all.

exhibits.title: Custody Memorandum — Umbral Signet (redacted copy)
exhibits.visual:
PORTAL ARTIFACT SET · ITEM 3 OF 4
function ·· shadow key
estate authority · umbral routing
custody
verified
A BLANK IS A CLAIM THAT AN ANSWER EXISTS
exhibits.onRecord: The publishable version. Function: shadow key, estate authority, umbral routing. Current custody and last verified date are blacked out. A full copy exists and will not be published, because [[roll:4|the enemy also reads the Waluipedia|stated as settled fact, not as a precaution. Somewhere in this archive there is a readership record that says so.|assume it; everyone does.]].
exhibits.analysis:
## What the redaction admits

Waluigi redacted two fields: **current custody** and **last verified**.

An adversary reading this page learns that the archive knows both. That is deliberate. A blank where an answer should be is a claim that the answer exists — and a bearer whose custody is publicly unknown but archivally recorded is much harder to rob than one whose name is printed.

What Waluigi cannot hide, because the memorandum states it plainly, is the *function*: shadow key, estate authority, umbral routing. Anyone reading this now knows the signet opens estates and moves people through shadow. Waluigi accepted that cost. [[roll:4|You cannot catalogue an artefact set and simultaneously pretend the artefacts do nothing|the honest cost of an honest archive. Every function published here is a function the opposition no longer has to discover.|a fair trade for a usable index.]].

## Item 3 of 4 — and the set is the point

The memorandum is headed *Portal Artifact Set · Item 3 of 4*, and clause one says the other three are catalogued in full.

So the archive is publishing three of four artefacts openly and hiding the custody of one. That is not caution. That is a **decoy structure**, and Waluigi will now confess to it in Waluigi's own file, because a decoy that the party does not understand is a decoy that the party will accidentally dismantle.

The set matters more than any member of it. Individually: a shadow key, an anchor key, a truth mirror, a fourth. Collectively: a *routing system* — authority to enter, an anchor to fix the far end, an instrument to verify what came through, and one more piece. Waluigi has been assuming for some weeks that the fourth item is the one that decides what a traveller **is** when it arrives, because every other function in the set is already covered and [[roll:5|that is the only job left|identity verification at the far end. Which is precisely what the Mirror of True Reflection does — and the mirror was found broken.|speculation dressed as deduction.]].

## Estate authority, and why that phrase is doing more work than it looks

*Estate authority.* Not *door-opening*. Not *access*. **Authority.**

A signet does not pick locks. A signet proves you are entitled. The Umbral Signet is not a burglary tool, it is a **credential** — and a credential is only meaningful inside a system that recognises it, which means there is a system, which means somebody maintains a register of who holds estate authority in the shadow, which means the estates are administered.

Administered by whom? Waluigi does not know. But hold it against the Feyward grafting page: *whoever keeps that record decides afterwards what happened.* Hold it against Shadeward, where a butler in a tuxedo materialised out of the dark and knew that Master Cornelius was expecting visitors who had arrived by accident from another plane.

A house does not *expect* an accident. Somebody sent notice ahead. Somebody with routing, credentials, and a register.

This is the closest thing this investigation has to a suspect, and it is not a person. It is a **clerical department**, and Waluigi finds that [[roll:6|considerably more frightening than a lich|departments keep hours, forms, and grievances. A grievance is the cheapest way into any administration ever built.|a colourful way of saying "we do not know".]].

docRolls.match: three keys open nothing
docRolls.success: the archive is publishing three of four on the explicit theory that a set is useless incomplete. That theory holds only while the fourth stays unlocated — which makes this document a bet, printed, with the stake named in it.
docRolls.failure: reasonable operational security.

exhibits.title: Carrier Discipline Order — Black Crystal
exhibits.secured: Issued after Lyranth demanded the crystal from Eager
exhibits.custody: Public-known carrier: Markop. Actual carrier: not recorded.
exhibits.visual:
who is carrying it · not established
ANCHOR KEY
exhibits.onRecord: Lyranth demanded the anchor key from Eager. Eager was not carrying it and [[roll:3|could not have produced it|Eager’s ignorance was genuine, which is why it was convincing. The best cover is the one the asset does not know he is running.|he did not have it. Nothing more to read.]]. The order exists to preserve that mistake.
exhibits.analysis:
## Two disasters, only one of which has happened

Clause I is the cleanest piece of counter-intelligence writing in the archive and Waluigi did not write it, which is why Waluigi is prepared to praise it.

“The enemy has established that the crystal matters. The enemy has **not** established who is carrying it. Those are two different disasters and only one of them has happened.”

Most parties, on being demanded an artefact, panic about the demand. The correct response is to audit what the demand *reveals about the demander*. Lyranth knew the crystal existed, knew it was with the party, and guessed wrong about the hand. That is a partial intelligence picture, and [[roll:5|a partial picture is a thing you can feed|feeding it requires knowing what the enemy already has. This order implies somebody has audited Lyranth’s knowledge and written it down.|easy to say, hard to do without being caught.]].

## Do not correct it accidentally, which is harder

Clause II instructs the party not to correct Lyranth's error, and then adds the clause that makes Waluigi trust the drafter: *do not correct it accidentally, either, which is harder.*

Deliberate silence is easy. Accidental correction is the real failure mode: Eager looking relieved, Markop patting the wrong pocket, someone saying *he doesn't have it* in a corridor where the walls have recently produced a Mystic Morel.

Markop is under standing instruction to be visibly, tediously careful with a pocket, and to keep being careful with that pocket long after it stops feeling necessary. That last part is the professional touch. Every amateur maintains a cover until the moment they relax, which is [[roll:4|the only moment anyone is watching|which means the watcher is patient and local. Not a raid — an observer, already inside the party’s routine.|general tradecraft, not a specific warning.]].

## Anchor key — the noun again

The subject line calls the Black Crystal an **anchor key**.

Waluigi asks the reader to go back to the Feyward key tag and the third layer of it. Anchor in the Shadowfell, holding a plane's condition over a house. Anchor in the Feyward, as a role a *person* can be made to fill. And here, in the party's own quartermaster paperwork, an object described as the key to one.

The party is carrying a component of the same system it is investigating. Nobody in the party phrased it that way, because the crystal arrived as loot and loot is not interrogated.

Waluigi is interrogating it. If the Black Crystal is an anchor key, then the question is not *who wants to steal it from us*. The question is **what is currently anchored, and does carrying the key make the bearer part of the mechanism**. Lyranth demanded it from Eager. Lyranth may not have been trying to acquire an artefact at all. Lyranth may have been trying to establish [[roll:6|which body the key was attached to|attached. Not "carried by". If a bearer can become part of the mechanism, the demand was a survey, and the survey succeeded.|a demand is usually just a demand.]].

docRolls.match: This error is the single most valuable asset the party currently owns
docRolls.success: an enemy's wrong belief filed as an asset, in an inventory, with an instruction not to correct it. The party is now running a deception it did not plan, through a man who does not know he is running it.
docRolls.failure: a fortunate mistake, and they know it.

docRolls.match: Not recorded here. That is the point.
docRolls.success: the archive that catalogues everything has deliberately left one field blank and said so. Compare the umbral signet memorandum, which redacts custody the same way. Two documents, one habit: the archive hides carriers, never objects.
docRolls.failure: an obvious precaution.

exhibits.title: Restoration Account — Mirror of True Reflection
exhibits.secured: Recovered broken from Usk's private chambers
exhibits.custody: Green T, at close of business
exhibits.onRecord: 650 gold, unpaid. Mending cast on a major artifact under field conditions, the absent fragment recovered and refitted, and a salvage claim entered by Wario — [[roll:3|verbally, immediately, twice|twice, in front of witnesses, before Akamatsu closed the account — which is why the strike had to be written onto the invoice instead of simply ignored. You cannot strike a claim that was never entered. Wario's two sentences forced a 650 gp working document to permanently record that Wario wanted the mirror, and that record is now Exhibit 8 in a case about who gets to hold the instrument that tells people apart.|Wario claims everything twice.]] — and struck.
exhibits.analysis:
## Salvage requires a wreck

R. Akamatsu struck Wario's claim with seven words: *Salvage requires a wreck. This was a repair.*

Waluigi is obliged to note that this is legally correct and that Wario knew it was legally correct when he entered the claim twice. The claim was not a legal argument. It was an attempt to establish a *timestamp* — a recorded moment at which Wario asserted interest in the mirror, so that a later negotiation could begin from “as previously claimed” rather than from nothing.

Wario does not win arguments. [[roll:4|Wario creates paper that other people have to argue against later|then check this file for the second instance, because there is one. Wario also moved on Steely's remains, and that claim was refused too — the construct was promised burial rather than salvage. Same verb, same week, two different objects: an artifact that identifies people, and the body of a party member. Both times Wario reached for the word *salvage*, and both times somebody had to spend words taking it back off the record.|an old habit, widely known.]]. Waluigi says this with professional affection and total distrust.

## The line item that is not about money

Third line of the account: *Handling of an object that shows the handler what they are. 200 gp.*

An artificer billed two hundred gold for the psychological cost of touching the thing. That line is not padding — it is above the fragment recovery in the itemisation, which means Akamatsu considered it the second most demanding part of the job.

The Mirror of True Reflection was found **broken** in Usk's private chambers, with a piece missing that had to be recovered separately. Waluigi would like the reader to consider the ordinary explanation, which is that it got knocked over, and then to consider the other one: that somebody who did not like the answer broke it, and then removed a specific fragment, and that [[roll:5|the fragment was not lost but *taken*|and it was recovered separately, by somebody, from somewhere. That recovery has no chain of custody anywhere in this file.|things break; pieces scatter.]].

## A different person has held it every time

The archive's own footnote: *the person holding the mirror of truth has been a different person every time.*

Waluigi added that line and Waluigi is now going to defend it, because it is the most useful sentence in the file about the party.

An instrument that verifies identity is only as trustworthy as its chain of custody, and this one has no chain — it has a *sequence of unrelated hands*. Usk had it broken. Akamatsu had it in pieces. Wario tried to have it before it set. Green T has it at close of business, and Green T is a person who counts revolver rounds out and back on a discipline sheet, which is the single strongest argument for leaving it exactly where it is.

In a case whose central mechanism is **replacing people with things wearing their line**, the party owns one device that can tell the difference and [[roll:5|has never once assigned it a permanent keeper|an instrument with no keeper has no baseline. Nobody can say whether it reads the same today as it did in Usk’s chambers.|it has stayed within the party. That is custody enough.]]. That is the operational recommendation this investigation most wants acted on, and Waluigi has no authority to give orders, only the ability to write them down where they are embarrassing.

docRolls.match: Handling of an object that shows the handler what they are
docRolls.success: Akamatsu billed 200 gold for the personal cost of touching it, itemised between mending and refitting like any other line. The artificer looked into a mirror of truth during the repair and charged for what it cost her.
docRolls.failure: artificers charge for hazard. Standard practice.

docRolls.match: Claim struck: the claimant did not break it and did not fix it
docRolls.success: Wario claimed salvage on an object that was never a wreck, twice, in front of witnesses. The strike is dated and the claim survives underneath it — which is exactly the outcome he wanted from claiming it at all.
docRolls.failure: the claim failed. The paperwork worked.

exhibits.title: Reading Register — Cards Drawn Against Events Occurring
exhibits.secured: Kept privately by Remi from the date of the gift
exhibits.visual:
×
RING
CARD LOGGED FIRST · OUTCOME LOGGED AFTER
exhibits.onRecord: Six draws. The right-hand column — what actually happened — was [[roll:4|filled in afterwards|the ordering is the whole evidentiary value. Reverse it and this document is worth nothing at all.|an ordinary way to keep a diary.]], which is the only honest way to keep such a record and the reason it is admissible.
exhibits.analysis:
## Why the method is sound and the result is worse for it

Remi recorded the card at the time and the outcome later. That ordering is everything. A prophecy log written after the fact proves nothing, because memory obligingly reshapes a vague card into a specific event.

So Waluigi cannot dismiss this the way Waluigi would like to.

*The Broken Window* — a window was broken, two days later. *The Guest Who Is Furniture* — a spy was found in a closet. Waluigi has tried to read those as retrofitted and cannot, because the cards were logged first, by a diligent person, in her own private book [[roll:4|with nobody to impress|a private book kept honestly is the hardest kind of evidence to dismiss and the easiest kind to steal from.|private books are still written by people.]].

## The Lady With Two Faces, left blank at the time

Third draw: *The Lady With Two Faces.* Recorded **before** the Feyward manor. Outcome column left blank at the time.

Remi drew a two-faced Lady before the party ever met a Lady who was not the Lady — before the cold tea, before the interview, before the Bob-omb, before a gold ring engraved OC fell out of the overgrowth.

Waluigi is not going to write *the deck predicted it*. Waluigi is going to write the sceptical version, which is somehow worse: **Morel gave Remi this deck.** Morel knew what was in the Feyward manor. A gift that produces an accurate card is a gift that was *loaded*, and a loaded deck is a way of putting information into a party without being the one who told them.

Either the cards are prophetic or Mystic Morel has been [[roll:6|running an intelligence channel through a card game|a channel needs a schedule. Compare the draw dates against Morel’s appearances — the register is dated and Morel is not subtle.|no way to distinguish the two readings from here.]]. Waluigi has no way to distinguish these and resents it.

## Draw five, draw six

Fifth draw: **—**. Card removed from deck. *Not by Remi.*

Sixth draw: **The Ring**. Outcome column deliberately empty. It has not happened yet.

Waluigi wants both of those understood together, because separately they are curiosities and together they are a threat assessment.

Somebody reached into the deck of a person who logs everything, removed a card, and did it cleanly enough that Remi could only record the absence. That is [[roll:5|the same operational signature as everything else in this file: not destruction, **editing**|editing implies the editor intends the record to keep being used. Nobody amends a document they mean to destroy.|theft is theft, however tidy.]]. The grafting page said watch who keeps the record. Here is somebody amending a record in the party's own pocket.

And the very next draw is *The Ring*, in an investigation where a ring is currently lodged with the Anvil with a person allegedly inside it.

The register's outcome column is the only blank space in this entire investigation that will fill itself in without anybody rolling for it. Waluigi advises the party to be present when it does.

docRolls.match: Card removed from deck. Not by Remi.
docRolls.success: somebody edited a prophetic deck between draws, and the register's keeper knew it was not her. The fifth future was not missed. It was taken out before it could be drawn.
docRolls.failure: decks lose cards. It happens.

docRolls.match: Recorded before the Feyward manor. Left blank at the time.
docRolls.success: The Lady With Two Faces was logged before anyone met a false Aurelian, and the outcome column was left honestly empty rather than filled in later. That blank is the reason this register is evidence and not a party trick.
docRolls.failure: a vague card and a convenient fit.

exhibits.title: Seal Rubbing — The Notation Kamek Read As An Invitation
exhibits.secured: Charcoal on paper, taken at the seal face · scale unrecorded
exhibits.visual:
“for me”
REPEATED WITHOUT VARIATION · CLOSED
exhibits.onRecord: Outer ring: binding notation, [[roll:4|repeated without variation|no variance means no keyhole. Whoever cut it was not planning to come back, which is itself a decision worth examining.|ward notation is not the archive’s field.]] — which in ward-work means closed. Middle ring: a dedication naming the thing sealed. Inner mark: annotated on the original, in a firm hand, “for me.”
exhibits.analysis:
## Repeated without variation means closed

The outer ring repeats one binding notation with no variation at all. Waluigi is not a ward scholar and has said so on the record. Waluigi has, however, had this confirmed: in ward-work, **repetition without variation is the notation for a closed condition**. A ward meant to be opened by a keyholder carries a variance — a break in the pattern where the key engages.

There is no variance anywhere on this rubbing.

The seal was not lockable. It was *sealed*, in the sense that a tomb is sealed, and the only correct reading of it was: [[roll:3|this stays shut|and it was read, by a literate wizard, and opened anyway. The failure was not literacy. It was appetite.|seals get broken. That is what seals are for.]].

## A dedication of the prison to what is inside it

The inner mark was read by the taker of the rubbing as a personal address. He wrote **“for me”** on the original, in a firm hand, in charcoal, next to a mark that dedicates a prison to its occupant.

The greatest wizard in Koopa history versus a label. The label lost first. Then everyone else did.

Waluigi has been careful throughout this file about mockery, because mockery is how an archive stops noticing things. So here is the non-mocking version. Kamek is not stupid and Kamek is not illiterate in ward-notation. Kamek read a dedication as an address because the notation is *ambiguous by design* — a mark that names the thing sealed will always be readable as a mark that names the reader, and [[roll:6|whoever cut that seal knew it|which makes the seal a trap with a very long fuse — built to be opened eventually, by whoever wanted it most.|ambiguity in old notation is common and usually accidental.]].

The seal was not merely a lock. It was a lock with **bait cut into the face of it**.

## Reading a document as saying what one wishes it said

The archive's closing note is Waluigi's own and Waluigi meant it as self-indictment: *Waluigi is extremely experienced in reading a document as saying what one wishes it said, and this is a textbook specimen.*

This is the methodological centre of the entire investigation, so Waluigi will spend a paragraph on it rather than a joke.

Every exhibit in this file can be read two ways. The key tag is a warning or an instruction. The grafting page is a confession or a boast. The reading register is prophecy or an intelligence channel. The ring contains Aurelian or contains a story the party badly wants to be true. In every single case the *pleasant* reading is available and free, and the unpleasant reading costs something.

Kamek picked the pleasant reading of one mark and it went the way it went.

So the standing rule of this investigation, written here because this is the exhibit that earns it: **when a document can be read two ways, [[roll:4|the archive files both, and marks which one the archive would prefer|Kamek wrote *for me* on a ward that says only *this stays shut*. He read an instruction as an invitation, dug under a castle on the strength of it, and woke the thing that ate his own troops. The archive prefers the reading that does not flatter the reader.|a good rule, stated once and hard to audit.]].** A preference that is written down can be checked by somebody else later. A preference that is not written down becomes a fact within about a fortnight.

docRolls.match: A dedication. Names the thing sealed, not the reader.
docRolls.success: the middle ring settles it in one line. The seal addresses its prisoner. Kamek read a label on a cage as a letter to himself, and dug under a castle on the strength of that reading.
docRolls.failure: ward notation is not the archive's field.

docRolls.match: Read by the taker of this rubbing as a personal address.
docRolls.success: the rubbing records its own reader's interpretation as part of the evidence. Whoever filed this understood that how Kamek read the seal is a more useful fact than what the seal says.
docRolls.failure: an annotation, dutifully noted.

exhibits.title: Ammunition Accountability Sheet
exhibits.secured: Ongoing · maintained by Green T personally
exhibits.visual:
recovered from the host
the tanuki matter
accounted: NO
ROUNDS UNACCOUNTED FOR · 0
exhibits.onRecord: Rounds out against rounds accounted. Every occasion balances. [[roll:3|One line is struck|struck, not erased. Somebody wanted the failure to remain legible to whoever audits the sheet next.|bookkeeping correction, presumably.]], and the struck line is the exhibit.
exhibits.analysis:
## Silver. Recovered from Orangus Cornelius. Yes.

Line one. *Dinner, the vampire. Out 6. Fired 1. Accounted: Silver. Recovered from Orangus Cornelius. Yes.*

Green T shot the host of a vampire dinner from the children's table, and then went and **got the bullet back**.

Waluigi wants that sequence appreciated properly. It is not bravado. Recovering the round means no silver ball is left in a Shadowfell estate for somebody to match to a weapon, and it means the sheet balances. A person who retrieves evidence from inside a host during an active incident is not a child at a children's table. [[roll:4|That is fieldcraft|fieldcraft is taught. Ask who taught it, because nobody in this party admits to running the lesson.|quick thinking under pressure, nothing trained.]].

## Weapon not loaded during instruction

*Instruction of R. Akamatsu. Out 6. Fired 0. Accounted: Yes — weapon not loaded during instruction.*

Green T logged six rounds out, taught an artificer to handle a revolver, fired nothing, and specified in the accounted column that the weapon was empty for the lesson.

Nobody required that note. The sheet already balanced without it. It is there because Green T holds themself to a standard nobody in this party has asked for and most of them could not meet.

Waluigi files this in an investigation about people being replaced by things wearing their faces, and here is why: **[[roll:5|this sheet is an identity document|then it is also a test. Hand a suspected graft a discipline sheet and watch whether it can be bothered to fill in the column nobody checks.|habits can be observed and copied.]].** Nothing in the Feyward or the Shadeward could counterfeit the habit of writing that line. A graft can wear a face. It cannot be bothered to note that the weapon was unloaded during a lesson that went fine.

## The line that cannot be totalled

*The tanuki matter — moral accounting. Out: —. Fired: —. Accounted: **No**.*

And underneath, in the archive's hand: *the struck line is struck because [[roll:5|it cannot be totalled, not because it was resolved|the only unresolved line in an archive full of confident conclusions, and it was left by the youngest person holding a gun.|some things do not tally. He left it open.]].*

Green T fired one round in the tanuki matter, accounted for it in the line above, and then opened a second line for the part that a rounds ledger has no column for. Then struck it. Not erased — **struck**, which leaves it legible.

Waluigi has spent this whole investigation arguing that whoever keeps the record decides what happened. Here is the counter-example, and Waluigi is glad to have it in the file. Green T kept a record that deliberately fails to resolve, in a format designed to always resolve, and left the failure visible.

That is what an honest archive looks like. Rounds unaccounted for: 0. Everything else: outstanding.

docRolls.match: Silver. Recovered from Orangus Cornelius. Yes.
docRolls.success: he went back for the round after it had been fired into a vampire. That is not tidiness — silver is evidence and it is expensive, and a fifteen-year-old with a silenced revolver worked out both without being told.
docRolls.failure: he kept his silver. Sensible.

docRolls.match: moral accounting
docRolls.success: he added a row to his own discipline sheet that no discipline sheet has a column for, then struck it because it would not total. Every round is accounted for. The tanuki is not.
docRolls.failure: an odd entry in an otherwise tidy ledger.

exhibits.title: Addendum — Why This Session Matters More Than It Looks
exhibits.secured: Attached to the session record · the session did not close the branch
exhibits.visual:
Toad Lee
security problem
Morel
informant
Steely
lost
the revel
ongoing
A LEGIBLE PROBLEM CAN BE HUNTED
exhibits.onRecord: Waluigi's argument that an unsolved problem you can finally see is worth more than a solved one. A solved problem stops moving. [[roll:3|A legible problem can be hunted|so apply it to the file itself and the count is uncomfortable. Of twelve exhibits, three exist only because somebody tried to make them stop existing — a key thrown into the dark, a fifth card lifted out of a spread, a salvage claim struck through. Every one of those removals is what made the thing legible. The method in this case does not destroy evidence. It edits it, and editing leaves a shape.|a slogan. Pleasant, but a slogan.]].
exhibits.analysis:
## Before and after, in four rows

The addendum's table is the closest thing the archive has to an honest progress report.

*Toad Lee:* useful and occasionally ridiculous → useful, ridiculous, **and a possible security problem**.

*Mystic Morel:* ambiguous presence → antagonist and informant, appeared from a wall, survived near-decapitation, issued a targeted warning, provided a key.

*Steely:* present → lost.

*The revel:* ongoing → still ongoing.

One of those four rows got worse, two got more detailed, and one did not move at all. [[roll:4|Waluigi published it in that order deliberately|worst first. The archive leads with the row that indicts the party, which is the only way the rest of it stays credible.|an order is just an order.]].

## Legibility as a war aim

“A solved problem stops moving. A legible problem can be hunted.”

Waluigi wrote that and then had to live with it, because it is the justification for this entire investigation existing instead of a quest board.

A quest board says *retrieve the item, receive the reward, the entry closes*. That model assumes the problem is a task. This is not a task. Nobody is going to hand the party a completed Feyward branch in exchange for enough chopping.

What the party can actually accumulate is **resolution** — in the optical sense. Every exhibit that gets examined makes the shape slightly sharper, and the shape is what you hunt. The XP in this file is not paid for defeating anything. It is paid for making something visible, because [[roll:5|visibility is the only thing in this campaign that has never once been taken back|and the file can prove it three times over. Wario's salvage claim was struck and is still readable under the strike. The fifth card was removed from the spread and the removal was itself written down. The key was thrown away and the throw became the exhibit. Every attempt in this investigation to unmake a fact has instead produced a dated, custodied record of the attempt — which is the one structural weakness in a method that works by controlling what the record says.|an optimistic claim from a pessimistic archivist.]].

## Obligations, evidence, and debts that never appear on a sheet

The addendum ends: *Money is not the only thing characters carry. They carry obligations. They carry evidence. They carry debts that never appear on a sheet.*

Waluigi will now inventory what the Feyward branch is carrying, since nobody else has.

**Obligations.** A ring lodged with the Anvil containing, allegedly, a person. A construct's remains that were promised burial rather than salvage. A Toad who is either a victim or a vector and has been told he is neither.

**Evidence.** Everything in this file. Twelve exhibits, in custody, with hands attached to each one.

**Debts that never appear on a sheet.** Morel is owed something for the key, and Morel will name the price at a moment of Morel's choosing. Akamatsu is owed 650 gold and has not pressed. [[roll:4|Aurelian is owed her body back|and the debt is owed by the party, who currently hold her in a ring, filed under Article, lodged with a smith.|owed by someone. The file does not say who.]].

None of that is on a quest board because a quest board cannot represent it. It is on this page because Waluigi's archive can, and because a debt that has been written down is considerably harder to walk away from than a debt that has merely been felt.

investigations.title: Who Signed, And In What
investigations.subtitle: Coronations were theatre; real power signed in blood not ink
investigations.hook: The Ashford spirit said the coronations were theatre. Waluigi believes him, which is the problem, because Waluigi wants to believe him.
investigations.imageCaption: There are a great many images of the capital. Not one of them shows anybody signing anything.
investigations.brief:
Waluigi is opening this file empty and saying so, because an empty file that admits it is empty is more honest than a full one that has been padded.

What exists: a spirit's testimony, relayed through notes that may or may not be Luigi's, stating that coronations were **theatre** while real power *signed in blood not ink*, and that documents are sealed in iron beneath a hanging tree in the Thornwood.

What does not exist: a single piece of paper from the capital in the archive's custody. Not one. Waluigi has an entire investigation's worth of Feyward stationery and nothing at all from the building where the decisions were made, which is itself a finding — the capital produces speeches and the Feyward produces evidence, and Waluigi would like the reader to notice which institution is more careful.

This file opens properly the day somebody brings back paper.

threads.title: Documents sealed in iron beneath a hanging tree
threads.text: Coordinates in the Thornwood, per the Ashford testimony. Unverified. Uninvestigated. Waluigi is aware of how that sentence looks in an archive that has been running for months.

leads.title: Recover the documents sealed in iron
leads.objective: Locate the hanging tree in the Thornwood and retrieve whatever is sealed beneath it in iron.
leads.why: It is the only physical evidence the succession thread has ever been offered, and it was offered by a spirit whose other statements are unfalsifiable. Iron and paper are falsifiable. Go and get them.

leads.title: Identify the third branch
leads.objective: Establish which branch of the succession the Ashford spirit meant by “broken at third branch,” and whether the break was an event or a procedure.
leads.why: Held against the Aurelian grafting page, *branch* stops being a genealogist's metaphor and becomes the same gardening vocabulary the Feyward uses for splicing a bloodline. If the capital's succession was grafted, the crisis has a mechanism instead of a mystery.

investigations.title: An Enormous Claim With No Custody Chain
investigations.subtitle: Divinity, asserted; paperwork, absent
investigations.hook: Several parties are hunting a god. Nobody has produced a document establishing that there is one.
investigations.imageCaption: Waluigi declines to illustrate a deity whose existence is the open question of the file.
investigations.brief:
Waluigi has a methodological objection to this entire subject and is going to lead with it.

Every other file in this archive begins with an article — a key, a ring, an invoice, a sheet of rusted components. This one begins with a **claim**, and the claim has been repeated so often and by so many that repetition has done the work custody should have done.

Waluigi's position: a god-toad is exactly the sort of proposition that produces action without evidence, which makes it exactly the sort of proposition somebody would manufacture. Waluigi is not saying it is false. Waluigi is saying the file stays a stub until somebody brings back something that can be put on a table.

The Kamek seal rubbing, filed in the SHADEWARD FEYWARD RUINED investigation, is the cautionary specimen: the greatest wizard in Koopa history read a dedication as a personal invitation because he wanted to. This file will not open on a want.

threads.title: Repetition is not custody
threads.text: The god-toad is attested by many mouths and no articles. Waluigi wants one physical thing — a seal, a register, a receipt for a sacrifice, anything with a hand attached to it.

leads.title: Obtain one physical article attesting the god-toad
leads.objective: Bring back a single object or document, with a chain of hands, that establishes the claim independently of anybody's testimony.
leads.why: Because this file cannot open without one, and because a movement this large that has generated no paperwork in months has either been extraordinarily careful or has nothing to file.

leads.title: Establish what Kamek believes he was invited to
leads.objective: Get Kamek on the record about the inner mark, in his own words, before the archive's reading hardens into the official one.
leads.why: Waluigi has published a reading of that rubbing that makes Kamek look foolish. Waluigi's standing rule requires filing both readings, and Waluigi has so far only filed Waluigi's.

investigations.title: Liberation Is A Logistics Problem
investigations.subtitle: The rescue was the easy part and everybody knew it at the time
investigations.hook: Liberated Toads have been counted, integrated, and housed on paper. Waluigi would like to see the paper.
investigations.imageCaption: Waluigi has seen the camp. Waluigi is not going to describe it in a caption.
investigations.brief:
This is the file Waluigi least wants to write and is therefore writing first among the stubs.

The liberation itself is well documented and genuinely creditable. What is not documented — at all, anywhere in this archive — is the **afterwards**: who is feeding them, under whose authority they are housed, what happens to a liberated Toad who wants to leave, and who is keeping *that* record.

Waluigi has spent an entire investigation arguing that whoever keeps the record decides afterwards what happened. That argument does not become less true when it is aimed at the party's own good deed. There are several hundred people whose status is currently defined by a system nobody in this archive has audited.

The file opens when somebody produces a roll, a ration ledger, or a housing register. Waluigi expects the ration ledger to be the interesting one. It always is.

threads.title: Nobody has audited the good deed
threads.text: Rescue generates narrative. Custody generates paperwork. This arc has produced a great deal of the former and none of the latter, and the people concerned are the ones who lose by that.

leads.title: Obtain the ration ledger
leads.objective: Get the actual feeding record for the liberated population — quantities, dates, and the name of whoever signs for it.
leads.why: A ration ledger cannot be rhetorical. It either balances or it does not, and if it does not, the discrepancy has a name at the bottom of it.

leads.title: Establish under whose authority they are housed
leads.objective: Identify the legal or practical basis on which the liberated Toads occupy where they occupy, and what happens if that basis is withdrawn.
leads.why: Estate authority turned out to be the load-bearing concept in the Shadeward file. Waluigi would like to check whether the party's own settlement rests on a credential somebody else can revoke.

investigations.title: What Was Actually Agreed
investigations.subtitle: A pact witnessed by many and written by none
investigations.hook: Everyone present agrees a pact was made at the Festival of the Fallen. No two accounts agree on its terms.
investigations.imageCaption: The festival was extensively observed and almost entirely unrecorded, which Waluigi suspects was arranged.
investigations.brief:
An oral pact is not a lesser instrument. Waluigi wants to be clear about that before the sceptical part, because in several cultures represented at that festival the spoken form is the binding one and the written form is the insult.

But an oral pact between parties who *do not share that convention* is a different animal. One side considers itself bound by what was said. The other considers itself bound by what was written, and nothing was written.

So the archive's question is not *was a pact made*. It is: **what does each party believe it owes**, and the two answers have never been placed side by side. Waluigi intends to place them side by side, in two columns, on one sheet, and then watch what happens to the room.

Stub until Waluigi has both columns.

threads.title: Two parties, two conventions, one unwritten agreement
threads.text: Nobody is lying yet. That is the window. Once one side acts on its own reading, somebody becomes a liar retroactively, and Waluigi would rather have the columns before that happens.

leads.title: Record both parties' understanding of the pact
leads.objective: Take each side's account of the terms separately, without letting either see the other, and file them in parallel columns.
leads.why: Separately is the only way it works. Together, the more forceful party's version becomes the record, and this archive has an entire investigation about what happens next when that occurs.

leads.title: Establish what was retrieved at Rogueport and for whom
leads.objective: Identify the retrieved article, its current custody, and whether it discharges any part of the pact.
leads.why: A retrieval performed under an unwritten agreement can be claimed afterwards as either a favour or a payment, and the difference is the whole alliance.
